_note: Life stages, births, aging and migration (DESIGN.md, Population growth). Days are game days; a game day is a real minute at 1x.

births._note: Births need a working clinic, a happy enough hole and a free bed.

school._note: Each unschooled child upsets their family (familySize people, child included): comfort falls in proportion, down to unschooledComfort when every family is affected.

elderCare._note: Elders without a place in elder care, plus someone looking after each, weigh on health.

migration._note: Once a day, adults in an unhappy hole may leave for a clearly happier one with free beds. They travel at rover speed.

death._note: Elders who pass away rest in a crypt. With no crypt space, grief weighs on comfort until it fades. Under 'Return to the soil' they become soil instead.

colonists._note: Individual colonists (#521, src/sim/colonists.ts). Ages are game days (a day is a month). assign: jobs go to the unemployed who live nearest. A bed is worth the home's niceness (its happiness target, in points) less the walk to work at metresPerPoint: a worker will walk metresPerPoint metres further for each point nicer (5: a home one comfort step, 8 points, nicer is worth 40 m more). The homeless take the free bed worth most to them; once a day anyone moves into a free bed worth moveGainPoints more, and two people swap beds after both would have gained swapGainPoints for swapAfterDays days running (each worker looks at the swapLooks homes worth most to them, from the nearestHomes nearest their job and the nicest). commute and foodWalk: comfort lost to a long walk to work or to the galley, nothing up to freeM metres, then comfortPerStep for each 10 m step past it, down to worstComfort.
